title: Dynamic Fidelity Metering and Offline Reconciliation Spec
author: Aisha Raman
content:
Overview

This design spec defines the requirements, data contracts, reconciliation algorithms, and rollout plan for dynamic fidelity metering and offline reconciliation. The goal is to produce a predictable, auditable metering record for fidelity-based consumption (per-request fidelity selection, fallback credits, and temporary fidelity degradations) that reconciles to customer billing and fidelity credits in cases where the online metering signal diverges from the final accounting state.

Why this doc exists
- Customers and finance teams require deterministic, explainable billing that reflects the fidelity the runtime delivered (including fallbacks and on-the-fly degradations).
- Real-time metering signals (edge/collector) will sometimes be incomplete, delayed, or reconciled by offline policies (e.g., model fallback, quantization rollbacks).
- We need a concise offline reconciliation algorithm and data model for crediting, refunds, and dispute resolution.

Goals
- Define the canonical event model for fidelity metering that the billing pipeline will consume.
- Specify reconciliation heuristics and thresholds to convert online telemetry to final invoiceable records.
- Provide test harness, simulation scenarios, and a staged rollout plan with safety gates.
- Minimize downstream finance adjustments by keeping divergence < 0.05% of monthly invoice amount for early pilots.

Scope and out-of-scope
- In scope: hosted inference and dedicated-internal routing (hosted and dedicated fleets using the fidelity API and fallback variants). Includes per-route flagging and variant credits.
- Out of scope: on-prem private deployments’ local billing agents (a separate adapter doc will be published).

High-level architecture (text diagram)
- Runtime -> Local collectors (edge) -> Event bus -> Real-time aggregator -> Billing reconciler (offline) -> Finance ledger
- When fallback/rollback occurs, runtime emits a 'finalization' event to trigger reconciliation.

Canonical event model (single-line JSON examples allowed in text)
- MeteringEvent (canonical fields):
  - request_id: unique request GUID
  - tenant_id: tenant account id
  - route_id: customer route identifier
  - timestamp: epoch ms of request start
  - seq_len: integer (tokens generated)
  - fidelity_tier: string (e.g., high, medium, low, quantized-v2)
  - variant_id: string (model variant used)
  - billed_tokens: integer (initial real-time token count)
  - meter_version: string (v1, v2)
  - finalized: boolean (false for streaming partials, true for final)
  - finalization_reason: string (e.g., normal, fallback, quantization-rollforward)
  - final_cost_units: decimal string (costable units after reconciliation)

Event contract notes
- All fields must be produced as strings or primitives by collectors even when empty to support robust downstream parsing.
- 'finalized' defaults to false; runtime must emit a finalized=true event within 30s if the request required fallback or variant substitution.

Reconciliation heuristics
1) Ideal path: online metering event is finalized and final_cost_units == billed_tokens * fidelity_multiplier -> mark settled.
2) Fallback correction: if runtime emitted finalization with finalization_reason=fallback, compute delta = final_cost_units - billed_tokens.
   - If delta < -0.01 tokens (more credit owed than billed), issue a negative invoice adjustment (credit) when monthly invoice is finalized.
   - If delta > 0.02 tokens (customer underbilled), flag for manual review if delta amount > $50; otherwise auto-charge in next invoice cycle.
3) Missing finalization: if no finalized event emitted within 120s, reconciliation will:
   - Use the last seen variant from real-time aggregator and apply a conservative fidelity multiplier (lowest fidelity) for invoiceable units; mark as 'provisional' until finalization arrives or backfill timeout (7 days) expires.
4) Inconsistent seq_len: if finalization seq_len differs from real-time recorded seq_len by >20% apply size normalization: prefer max(seq_len_real_time, seq_len_final) unless finalization explicit_reason indicates truncation.

Thresholds and SLOs
| Metric | Target | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Real-time finalization latency | <= 30s (90p) | Emit finalized=true within 30s after request end for fallback/variant events. |
| Reconciliation divergence (monthly $) | < 0.05% | Pilot target across customers. |
| Auto-adjustment threshold | $50 | Above this, route to billing review queue. |
| Backfill window | 7d | After this, provisional amounts become final with conservative policy. |

Offline reconciliation algorithm (stepwise)
1. Ingest all MeteringEvent records for the invoice window ordered by request_id and timestamp.
2. Group by request_id, collapse duplicates; prefer events where finalized=true.
3. For each request: determine final_cost_units as follows:
   a. If finalized=true and final_cost_units provided -> use final_cost_units.
   b. Else if finalized=false but matching post-fact finalization event exists in backfill -> use that.
   c. Else use real-time billed_tokens * conservative_fidelity_multiplier (configured per-tenant).
4. Compute delta = final_cost_units - billed_tokens (from real-time). Store reconciliation_delta in ledger entry.
5. If |delta| * token_price > auto_adjust_threshold -> create billing-review ticket and attach event payloads.
6. Otherwise, auto-apply credit/debit in next invoice cycle and emit AdjustmentEvent.

Simulation scenarios and test harness
- Harness: a simulator that replays runtime behavioral traces with variable fallback rates, network drops, and collector delays.
- Minimum scenarios:
  1) 0% fallback, 95th finalization latency 4s -> expect divergence <0.005%
  2) 12% fallback to lower-fidelity variant with immediate finalization -> expect credits applied automatically
  3) 0.5% collector drop (missing events) with 10% backfill resolution within 48h -> provisional accounting exercised
  4) 1% of requests with truncation and inconsistent seq_len -> reconciliation chooses max(seq_len,final_seq_len) rule

Configuration table (per-tenant defaults; can be overridden by contract)
| config_key | default | description |
|---|---:|---|
| conservative_fidelity_multiplier | 0.7 | Multiplier applied when no finalization exists (percent of expected token cost). |
| backfill_window_days | 7 | Days to wait for finalization/backfill before settling provisional entries. |
| auto_adjust_threshold_usd | 50 | Monetary threshold for manual review. |
| finalize_latency_threshold_s | 30 | Maximum recommended latency for finalized events. |

Edge cases and dispute resolution
- Duplicate events: dedupe by request_id + meter_version; if conflicts remain escalate to manual review.
- Corrupted events: if critical fields missing, mark as 'malformed' and route to data-quality team; do not auto-charge.
- Retroactive model change: if a model variant is later invalidated (e.g., safety rollback), issue a retroactive reconciliation job for affected window and flag for customer communication.

Observability and dashboards
- Key dashboards:
  - Finalization latency heatmap (by tenant, route)
  - Monthly divergence by tenant (USD and %)
  - Backfill queue depth and resolution time
  - Manual review queue and RCA tags
- Alerting:
  - Pager when overall divergence > 0.2% in a 24h window (oncall: eng-platform).
  - Pager when backfill_queue_depth > 100k requests unresolved > 48h (oncall: eng-infra).

Rollout plan and guardrails
1. Canary (2 customers): enable real-time finalization emission and run offline reconciler in dry-run mode for 14 days. Validate divergence, finalize thresholds.
2. Pilot cohort (20 customers): enable auto-adjust with conservative thresholds and finance review. Run 60-day evaluation and collect disputes.
3. General availability: enable auto-adjust for all hosted customers with contracts permitting auto billing adjustments; provide opt-out for customers requiring manual monthly reconciliation.

Migration and backwards compatibility
- Metering v1 -> v2 adapter: the offline reconciler will accept v1 events and synthesize missing finalized fields using conservative defaults.
- Existing billing consumers must accept AdjustmentEvent messages and ledger entries tagged with 'reconciled'.

Operational runbook (summary)
1. If divergence spike detected: check finalization latency dashboard -> inspect top 10 tenants by divergence -> query raw MeteringEvent traces for those tenants -> escalate to runtime oncall if fallback/finalization floods are observed.
2. If backfill queue grows: trigger prioritized backfill worker pool with tenant-aware rate limiting.
3. For a disputed invoice: attach reconciliation delta report and request_id list; create finance dispute ticket and initiate manual correction flow.

Appendix A — Example event payloads
- Real-time event (example):
{
  "request_id": "req_3f9c2a",
  "tenant_id": "acct_44",
  "route_id": "route-payments",
  "timestamp": "1720641234000",
  "seq_len": "128",
  "fidelity_tier": "high",
  "variant_id": "v1.3-opt",
  "billed_tokens": "130",
  "meter_version": "v2",
  "finalized": "false"
}

- Finalized event (example after fallback):
{
  "request_id": "req_3f9c2a",
  "finalized": "true",
  "finalization_reason": "fallback",
  "seq_len": "124",
  "final_cost_units": "90"
}

Appendix B — CLI utilities
- reconciliation dry-run: ./reconciler --window=2026-06-01_2026-06-30 --dry-run
- produce reconciliation report: ./reconciler --report --tenant=acct_44 --window=2026-06-01_2026-06-30

Open questions
- Should we expose finalization latency per-route to customers in the Console? (tradeoff: exposes runtime internals but useful for troubleshooting).
- Do we allow customers to configure auto_adjust_threshold_usd per-contract during onboarding? (recommended yes for enterprise)

Next steps
1. Alignment: review with Eng-Platform, Finance Integrations, and Legal for audit requirements (target: 2026-08-06).
2. Prototype: implement backfill worker and reconciliation job in dry-run by 2026-09-01.
3. Canary: onboard two pilot tenants and measure divergence for 14 days.
